doc.title: Malignant hyperthermia
doc.story: A fit 35-year-old man on the table, breathing room air: premedicated with midazolam and fentanyl, preoxygenated, induced with propofol and succinylcholine, intubated and maintained on sevoflurane 2 %. The jaw is stiff after the succinylcholine. Minutes into surgery the EtCO₂ rises at unchanged ventilation when it should be falling (42 → 45; without MH it settles at 36–39), with a rising heart rate (64 → 80, blunted by fentanyl); untreated on this build, the core temperature rises slowly (about 37.3 °C at 51 minutes) and the established state comes only after about 100 minutes; the arrest branch is not reached on the demo path. Run the MH crisis: trigger off with a propofol infusion in its place, oxygen, hyperventilation, dantrolene (again if the EtCO₂ climbs back), cooling above 38.5 °C and the potassium.

objectives.text: Name malignant hyperthermia from the monitor: EtCO₂ rising at unchanged ventilation when it should be falling (42 → 45; without MH it settles 36–39) with a rising heart rate (64 → 80, blunted by fentanyl) (instructor-assessed)
Call the MH crisis (stop sevoflurane, charcoal filters, propofol infusion, O₂ 100 % at 10 L/min, hyperventilate) within 120 s of the early signs (EtCO₂ past 45 mmHg at unchanged ventilation)
Give dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg within 300 s of calling the crisis
The EtCO₂ is climbing back at normal ventilation: the MH is not controlled — second dose of dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg and hyperventilate again (20 × 600, O₂ 100 %)
Treat the potassium (calcium chloride, insulin with dextrose) within 300 s of K⁺ rising above 5.5 mmol/L
Hyperventilation kept until EtCO₂ has stayed below 40 mmHg for 2 min, then ventilation normalised (back to 12 × 500)

takeHome: A rising EtCO₂ at the same ventilation with a rising heart rate: think of MH early.
Trigger off, 100 % oxygen at high flow, hyperventilation, and dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg.
Keep hyperventilating until the EtCO₂ stays down; if it climbs again, repeat dantrolene.
After the crisis: ICU 24–48 h, dantrolene 1 mg/kg every 4–6 h for 24 h (recrudescence in up to 50 %), then referral for testing and family counselling.
doc.notes: Showcase case (Stage 11; the induction sequence E119, 2026-10-24). MODELED: the physiology produces every change; the buttons only give what their label says. Oxygen is never implicit (E121): he breathes room air until Preoxygenate (face mask, 100 %), and the ventilator FiO₂ 0.5 comes with Intubate; induce without Preoxygenate and the apnoea before the tube desaturates. The MH condition starts at the succinylcholine (Induce); on this sequence the early signs come about 4.5 min after it (the hypoventilation after the premedication and the apnoea at induction raised the CO₂ stores; on the ventilator the EtCO₂ should then fall, and it rises instead). The trigger-off step starts a propofol infusion 100 µg/kg/min in place of the sevoflurane; the charcoal filters it names are not modelled (the vaporiser at 0 % with 10 L/min fresh gas washes the agent out). The cooling step gives the saline at the theatre's 21 °C: the engine has no input for refrigerated fluid. The second dantrolene answers the EtCO₂ climbing back at normal ventilation, and it puts the crisis ventilation back (20 × 600 at 100 % O₂: owner, 2026-10-28); ventilation returns to 12 × 500 again only after the EtCO₂ has stayed below 40 for 2 min, the rule of the first return, never on a timer: the same button in Recovering, pressed on that rule. The Debrief judges the first return only (objective 6); a seventh objective for the second would not fit the report's page 1 (B6 f: 274 mm against 267). Measured course and bands: docs/plans/stage-11-scenarios.md; this sequence: the E119 rows of docs/showcase/SHOWCASE-2-RUN-SHEET.md.

states.notes: Say it: the jaw is hard to open after the succinylcholine (masseter rigidity). The monitor cannot show it. In practice a rigid jaw after succinylcholine means a non-triggering anaesthetic from now on and close watch of the EtCO₂; today the volatile stays to show the crisis. Masseter rigidity with a rising EtCO₂ makes two signs.
